title: Fourier formula for flip correlation
statement:
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $S\subseteq[n]$. If $x^S$ denotes the vector obtained from $x$ by flipping exactly the coordinates in $S$, then
\[
\E_x[f(x)f(x^S)] = \sum_{T\subseteq[n]}(-1)^{|T\cap S|}\widehat f(T)^2,
\]
where $\widehat f(T)=\E_x[f(x)\chi_T(x)]$ and $\chi_T(x)=\prod_{i\in T}\sigma(x_i)$.
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and equip $\{0,1\}^n$ with its uniform probability measure; write $\mathbb E$ for uniform expectation. For $S\subseteq[n]$, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for real cube functions $h$. For $S\subseteq[n]$, let $x^S$ be the bit vector obtained by flipping exactly the coordinates in $S$. For every real cube function $f$ and $S\subseteq[n]$, $\mathbb E[f(x)f(x^S)]=\sum_{T\subseteq[n]}(-1)^{|T\cap S|}\widehat f(T)^2$.
